fixes.row: Given through Moses; set before the people; “the Law of Moses”
fixes.why: The label says the law was given through Moses, but its example Gal 3:19 says the law was administered through angels by a mediator, and Acts 7:53 says it was ordained by angels; Moses is not named in either. The label states one reading of a verse that names none. The note already says so, but the label and the example do not match.
fixes.fix: Relabel to “Given and set before the people; “the Law of Moses”” and replace example Gal 3:19 with Exod 24:12 (Berean: the LORD said to Moses, I will give you the tablets with the law). Keep Gal 3:19 and Acts 7:53 in the row and in the note.

fixes.why: Example Rom 3:27 prints “principle” in the Berean and no word for law, so the row’s own example does not show its label. The faith-and-law question is the one these two traditions most read this row for.
fixes.fix: Replace example Rom 3:27 with Rom 3:28 (“a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law”). Keep Rom 3:27 in the verses and in the note.

fixes.row: Jesus speaks of the law: “I have not come to abolish”, “in your own Law”, “not one of you keeps it”
fixes.why: Its label quotes “in your own Law”, which none of the four examples shows. Luke 24:44 is shown instead, and it does not contain any of the label’s quoted phrases.
fixes.fix: Replace example Luke 24:44 with John 8:17 (Berean: “Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid”). Keep Luke 24:44 in the verses and the note.

fixes.why: Example Luke 24:44 reads “the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms”, so it does not show the label’s phrase “The Law and the Prophets”.
fixes.fix: Replace example Luke 24:44 with Acts 13:15 (“After the reading from the Law and the Prophets”), which is already in the row’s verses.

fixes.why: The door the_prophets is named “Isaiah the prophet” (also in the leads). The row covers the prophets as a body, so the door names one prophet for all of them.
fixes.fix: Rename the door and the lead entry for the_prophets to “the prophets”.

fixes.row: Taught and read aloud; the priests, Levites, scribes and Pharisees
fixes.why: The label names the priests, the Levites, the scribes and the Pharisees, but none of the four examples names any of them (Acts 13:15 shows only the reading). Half of the label is shown by no example.
fixes.fix: Replace example Acts 13:15 with Neh 8:7 (Berean: “The Levites … instructed the people in the Law”), which is already in the row’s verses.

fixes.row: Taught and read aloud; the priests, Levites, scribes and Pharisees
fixes.why: Matt 23:23 (“you have disregarded the weightier matters of the law”) is a rebuke of the scribes and Pharisees. Placed in the row about the law being taught and read aloud, under a label naming the Pharisees, it reads as the Pharisees’ indictment inside the Torah row, which tilts the Torah’s own teaching toward a verdict on the group. It is the text’s rebuke, and a fair row says so.
fixes.fix: Move Matt 23:23 out of this row into “Jesus speaks of the law”, where it is Jesus speaking. Keep the Pharisees door and name in this row, and keep Rom 2:17 to 2:20 here.

fixes.row: Instruction and teaching: a father's, a mother's, a priest's, God's
fixes.why: Example Prov 13:14 reads “the teaching of the wise”, which none of the label’s possessives names (father, mother, priest, God). The label names a fixed set of speakers that the text does not keep to.
fixes.fix: Relabel to “Instruction and teaching: a father’s, a mother’s, a priest’s, the wise’s, God’s”. Optionally swap example Prov 13:14 for Prov 6:20 (Berean: “keep your father’s commandment, and do not forsake your mother’s teaching”), which is in the row’s verses.

fixes.row: Other “laws” the text names: of faith, of sin and death, of the Spirit of life, of Christ, of freedom, the royal law, of marriage
fixes.why: The label says “of faith”, but the Berean never says “law of faith”: Rom 3:27 prints “principle”, and the “law of faith” is only the Greek. Rule 1 requires that a label say only what its verses say. The note already explains the Greek.
fixes.fix: Remove “of faith” from the label. Keep Rom 3:27 and 7:21 in the row, with the note saying the Greek is νόμος and the Berean prints “principle”.

fixes.row: Judged by the law; brought to court
fixes.why: The note quotes John 19:7 (“according to that law He must die”) and the first half of John 18:31, but leaves out the second half, where the Jews say “We are not permitted to execute anyone.” The text supplies that context, and without it the row can read as the Jewish law itself condemning Jesus. The rabbi may object to missing context the text gives, and the young believer to a presentation that does not handle the passion narrative with care.
fixes.fix: Add to the note the whole of John 18:31 as the Berean gives it: “You take Him and judge Him by your own law,” Pilate told them. “We are not permitted to execute anyone,” the Jews replied.

fixes.row: “This is the law of ...”: the offerings, clean and unclean, childbirth, jealousy, the Nazirite
fixes.why: The note says the point of “the three rows at the end” is whether the rulings are fulfilled, ended or continued. Those three rows (21 to 23) are not at the end; rows 24 and 25 follow them. A reader checking the note finds it does not match the page.
fixes.fix: Change “the three rows at the end” to “the three rows below, after Other laws”.

fixes.why: The card is named “instruction” on the site, and the sense “instruction” is one of 26 verses out of 366. Twenty-four of the 25 rows are the law sense. Rule 4 says one sense of a word is never presented as its whole, and the card name does exactly that.
fixes.fix: Name the card “law (Torah) and instruction”, or match the card name to its title “What the text says of the law”.

fixes.why: Examples Job 36:10 (“correction”) and Prov 1:2 (“discipline”) show neither label word, so they do not show the section’s label.
fixes.fix: Replace Job 36:10 and Prov 1:2 with Prov 1:3 (Berean: “receiving instruction in wise living”) and Prov 1:8 (“your father’s instruction”).

fixes.why: Example Esth 1:8 (“By order of the king, no limit was placed on the drinking”) shows no word for law, edict or custom, so it does not show its label.
fixes.fix: Replace Esth 1:8 with Esth 3:8 (Berean: “Their laws are different from everyone else’s, and they do not obey the king’s laws”).

fixes.why: Example Job 11:4 reads “My doctrine is sound”. “Doctrine” is a claim about doctrine, not the teaching the section names, and a reader from either tradition would take it as a doctrinal word on the page.
fixes.fix: Replace Job 11:4 with Prov 4:2, which is in the word’s verses. Check the Berean reads “teaching” or “instruction” there before the swap.

fixes.why: The gloss shown for this word is MACULA’s “(Hall of) Judgment”, which is not a rendering a reader would recognise and reads as an odd sense. Example 2 Kgs 17:26 (“the requirements of the God of the land”) does not show law, instruction or teaching, and this word is an ordinance and a justice, not a law.
fixes.fix: Drop the MACULA gloss from the page for this word, and replace 2 Kgs 17:26 with Prov 1:3 (Berean: “justice”, the word the page keeps as ordinance).

worker_points.point: Contested point 1(a): the order A, D, N and the weight of the labels; the report says the middle label has six phrases
worker_points.why: The order is alphabetical by label, stated on the page, and the labels are set side by side with no ranking. The middle label, “Died to the law…”, is the longest by characters, but it has four quoted phrases, not six, and the report’s count is wrong.

worker_points.point: Contested point 1(b): Rom 10:4 and τέλος (end, goal or completion)
worker_points.why: The note gives the Greek word, lists its senses and says readers part on which Paul means, without choosing.

worker_points.point: Contested point 1(c): whether Gal 3:24 (guardian) belongs with the row of the law in time or with the row of its ending
worker_points.why: It is in the row of the law in time only, which is where its words are. The ending row does not take Gal 3:25, which has no law word, so nothing is cut apart.

worker_points.point: Contested point 1(d): no row names law-and-gospel, the third use, or a dispensation
worker_points.why: Checked against the labels and notes: none uses those terms or names a scheme.

worker_points.point: Contested point 2: faith, works, grace rows (15 to 17)
worker_points.why: The faith row’s example Rom 3:27 shows “principle”, not law (fix 2). The works and grace rows show their labels in all four examples. Whole-verse membership for Rom 3:28 and Gal 2:16 in both faith and works is stated and is the text’s own pairing.
All four examples show “under law” or “under the law”. The note quotes 1 Cor 9:20 as the Berean gives it, and takes no side on who is under the law.

worker_points.point: Contested point 4(a): row 11 shows that the Torah word is “instruction and teaching” in Proverbs, Isaiah, Malachi and Exodus 16, and one word, not two
worker_points.why: The Berean prints “law” in several verses of this word (Isa 8:16, 8:20, Jer 18:18, Hos 8:12, Mal 2:9), and the note says so. The row is kept by the word and not by the English, as the rabbi’s seat needs. The label needs only the possessive fix (fix 8).

worker_points.point: Contested point 4(b): row 12 (This is the law of …) as particular rulings; no row says they are ended
worker_points.why: The four examples show “This is the law of …” or “the law for …”, and the note names no scheme.

worker_points.point: Contested point 4(c): row 10 (native and foreigner; the nations; Gentiles)
worker_points.why: The examples show the foreigner (Exod 12:49, Num 15:29) and the Gentiles (Rom 2:14), and the Isa 2:3 example says “many peoples”, which the label covers. The note takes no side on Gentile believers.

worker_points.point: Contested point 4(d): row 9 puts Jer 31:33 with Heb 8:10, 10:16 and Rom 2:15 under one note on the new covenant
worker_points.why: All four examples show the heart or mind. The Hebrews quotations are the Greek quoting Jeremiah, which the row keeps as the text has them, and the note takes no side on whom the covenant is said to.
The label says “of faith”, which the Berean does not print (fix 9). The rest of the label is shown by its examples.

worker_points.point: Contested point 6: divine persons by hand
worker_points.why: Rule 3 says the divine persons are by hand, never by an inferred rule. Row 1 (The law of the LORD, of God) is built by adjacency to the divine words, which include κύριος (Lord). In the NT that word is Jesus in places, and Rom 7:25 (in row 1’s verses) reads “through Jesus Christ our Lord”. Make row 1 a hand list of verses, as Jesus’s row 24 already is. Its current membership is correct; the rule is what needs to change.

worker_points.point: Contested point 7: Heb 9:19, Acts 7:53 and Gal 3:19 (ordained or administered by angels) in the Moses row
worker_points.why: The label “Given through Moses” and the example Gal 3:19 do not match (fix 1). The three verses stay in the row, and the note keeps them as the text has them.

examples_checked: 96 of 100 rows' examples show their label; 4 do not: Gal 3:19 (under “Given through Moses”), Rom 3:27 (under “The law, and faith”), and Luke 24:44 (under both “The Law and the Prophets” and “Jesus speaks of the law”). Row 8 and row 11 show their label headings but not every possessive or group in them.
summary: The hub holds the text’s own words, keeps the instruction sense in a row of its own, and sets the three contested rows side by side with the same no-side note; it is fair to the Hebrew Scriptures and the rabbi’s seat has little to object to beyond missing context in the John 18:31 note. It ships after 16 fixes, mostly examples that do not show their label, a label that says more than its verses (Gal 3:19 and “of faith”), and a card name “instruction” for a hub that is mostly law.
